title: Grid
summary: A responsive grid is the standard LazyVerticalGrid with GridCells.Adaptive, and a short grid inside a scrolling screen is a FlowRow, with gaps from the Monarch space scale. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: LazyVerticalGrid with GridCells.Adaptive(minSize) for card grids and tiles that can be long: as many columns as fit items of that width. GridCells.Fixed(n) for a set number of columns. FlowRow with maxItemsInEachRow and weight(1f) for a few tiles inside a screen that already scrolls.
whenNotToUse: For a single wrapping row of chips or tags use FlowRow without a column count (see inline). For a table with aligned columns, headers and sorting use a data grid.
api: @Composable fun LazyVerticalGrid(columns: GridCells, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, state: LazyGridState = rememberLazyGridState(), contentPadding: PaddingValues = PaddingValues(0.dp), reverseLayout: Boolean = false, verticalArrangement: Arrangement.Vertical = ..., horizontalArrangement: Arrangement.Horizontal = Arrangement.Start, ..., content: LazyGridScope.() -> Unit)

@Composable inline fun FlowRow(modifier: Modifier = Modifier, horizontalArrangement: Arrangement.Horizontal = Arrangement.Start, verticalArrangement: Arrangement.Vertical = Arrangement.Top, itemVerticalAlignment: Alignment.Vertical = Alignment.Top, maxItemsInEachRow: Int = Int.MAX_VALUE, maxLines: Int = Int.MAX_VALUE, content: @Composable FlowRowScope.() -> Unit)

states.name: empty
states.description: Show MonarchEmptyState in place of the grid.

appearance: No appearance of its own: the items are Monarch components; the gaps are steps of the space scale.
platformNotes: The web's Grid takes minItemWidth (default 16rem), column counts per breakpoint, a gap from the space scale (default 16px) and fit or fill. On Android minItemWidth is GridCells.Adaptive(minSize), which behaves like the web's fit: columns stretch to share the width. Columns per breakpoint become GridCells.Fixed with a count chosen from the window size class. The gap is horizontalArrangement and verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(MonarchTheme.spacing.space4). A lazy grid cannot sit inside a vertical scroll of the same direction; FlowRow can. iOS uses LazyVGrid with adaptive GridItems.
accessibility: System behavior: TalkBack moves through the cells in reading order, row by row, and reports the collection size of a lazy grid.
Items that have not been composed are reached by scrolling, which TalkBack does as it moves.
edgeCases: A LazyVerticalGrid inside verticalScroll throws because it would be measured with infinite height; give it a bounded height or make it the screen's scrolling container.
At font scale 2.0 items grow taller; Adaptive keeps the columns, so keep minSize wide enough for the text.
